title.zh: 卷三十一 志第二十一 天文一
title.raw: 卷三十一 志第二十一 天文一 Volume 31 Treatises 25: Astronomy 1

sentences.zh: 昔者，堯命羲、和，出納日月，考星中以正四時。

translations.literal: In antiquity, Yao charged Xi and He to receive and give forth the sun and moon, examine the stars at culmination, and rectify the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, Emperor Yao appointed Xi and He to observe the passage of the sun and moon, determine the stars at their meridian transits, and thereby set the four seasons aright.

sentences.zh: 至舜，則曰「在璿璣玉衡，以齊七政」而已。

translations.literal: When it came to Shun, he only said, "Be present at the armillary sphere and jade transverse, to adjust the seven regulators."
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Shun, the charge had been reduced to the single injunction: "Take your place at the armillary sphere and jade level, and align the seven luminaries."

sentences.zh: 雖二典質略，存其大法，亦由古者天人之際，推候占測，為術猶簡。

translations.literal: Although the two canons are plain and brief, they preserve the great principle; it is also because in antiquity, at the juncture of Heaven and man, prognostication and observation for calendrical reckoning were still a simple art.
translations.idiomatic: Though the two canonical books are terse, they preserve the essential method; in early times, when heaven and humanity met in calendrical practice, prognostication and celestial observation remained comparatively simple arts.

sentences.zh: 至於後世，其法漸密者。

translations.literal: As for later ages, their methods gradually grew more refined.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, however, the methods grew steadily more exacting.

sentences.zh: 必積眾人之智，然後能極其精微哉。

translations.literal: One must surely accumulate the wisdom of many men before one can reach the utmost refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Only by gathering the wisdom of many minds could one approach their full subtlety.

sentences.zh: 蓋自三代以來詳矣。

translations.literal: From the Three Dynasties onward it has been detailed indeed.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Dynasties onward, the record grows richly detailed.

sentences.zh: 詩人所記，婚禮、土功必候天星。

translations.literal: What the poets record: for marriage rites and earthworks one must await the heavenly stars.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Poetry shows that wedding ceremonies and earthworks alike had to wait upon the stars.

sentences.zh: 而《春秋》書日食、星變，《傳》載諸國所占次舍、伏見、逆順。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals record solar eclipses and stellar anomalies; the Commentary records what the various states calculated concerning lodges, concealment and appearance, and retrograde and direct motion.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals note solar eclipses and irregularities among the stars, while the Commentary records how the various states computed stellar lodges, occultations, and the planets' retrograde and direct courses.

sentences.zh: 至於《周禮》測景求中、分星辨國、妖祥察候，皆可推考，而獨無所謂璿璣玉衡者，豈其不用於三代耶？

translations.literal: As for the Rites of Zhou — measuring shadow to seek the center, dividing stars to distinguish states, and inspecting portents and omens — all can be traced and verified, yet there is nowhere any mention of the so-called armillary sphere and jade transverse: was it not used in the Three Dynasties?
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou describe measuring the gnomon shadow to find the terrestrial center, mapping the stars to distinguish the realms, and scrutinizing prodigies and portents — all of which can be reconstructed in detail — yet nowhere mention the armillary sphere and jade level. Were these instruments not employed in the Three Dynasties after all?

sentences.zh: 抑其法制遂亡，而不可復得耶？

translations.literal: Or did their institutions perish so that they could never be recovered?
translations.idiomatic: Or had their design been lost beyond recovery?

sentences.zh: 不然，二物者，莫知其為何器也。

translations.literal: If not, then for these two objects no one knows what sort of instruments they were.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, no one today knows what those two instruments actually were.

sentences.zh: 至漢以後，表測景晷，以正地中，分列境界，上當星次，皆略依古。

translations.literal: From the Han onward, tables were used to measure the shadow and gnomon, to establish the terrestrial center, divide boundaries, and match above with the stellar lodges — all following the ancients in broad outline.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han dynasty onward, observers used marked tables and shadow measurements to fix the terrestrial center, parcel out territorial boundaries, and align them with the celestial mansions — all in rough accord with antiquity.

sentences.zh: 而又作儀以候天地，而渾天、周髀、宣夜之說，至於星經、曆法，皆出於數術之學。

translations.literal: Moreover they fashioned instruments to observe Heaven and Earth; the theories of the Armillary Heaven, the Zhou Bi, and the Clarified Night, as well as star manuals and calendrical methods, all issued from the study of number and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: They also built observational instruments for heaven and earth; doctrines such as the Armillary Heaven, Zhou Bi, and Clarified Night theories, together with star catalogs and calendrical systems, all arose from the mathematical sciences.

sentences.zh: 唐興，太史李淳風、浮圖一行，尤稱精博，後世未能過也。

translations.literal: When Tang arose, the Grand Astrologer Li Chunfeng and the monk Yixing were especially praised as profound and comprehensive; later ages could not surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang rose to power, Grand Astrologer Li Chunfeng and the monk Yixing were celebrated above all for their mastery; later generations have never surpassed them.

sentences.zh: 故采其要說，以著於篇。

translations.literal: Therefore their essential doctrines are gathered and set down in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Their principal teachings are therefore excerpted and recorded in this treatise.

sentences.zh: 至於天象變見所以譴告人君者，皆有司所宜謹記也。

translations.literal: As for celestial appearances and anomalies by which Heaven admonishes rulers, the responsible officials ought diligently to record them.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial anomalies by which Heaven warns rulers are likewise matters that responsible officials should scrupulously document.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，淳風上言：「舜在璿璣玉衡，以齊七政，則渾天儀也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Chunfeng submitted a memorial: "When Shun was at the armillary sphere and jade transverse to adjust the seven regulators, that was the armillary celestial instrument."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign, Chunfeng memorialized the throne: "Shun's charge to take his place at the armillary sphere and jade level and align the seven luminaries refers to the armillary celestial instrument."

sentences.zh: 《周禮》，土圭正日景以求地中，有以見日行黃道之驗也。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the earth gnomon rectifies the solar shadow to seek the terrestrial center — evidence by which one may see the sun's travel along the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou prescribe using the earth gnomon to correct the solar shadow and find the terrestrial center — proof that the ancients could observe the sun's motion along the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 暨於週末，此器乃亡。

translations.literal: By the end of the Zhou, this instrument perished.
translations.idiomatic: By the close of the Zhou dynasty, the instrument had been lost.

sentences.zh: 漢落下閎作渾儀，其後賈逵、張衡等亦各有之，而推驗七曜，並循赤道。

translations.literal: In Han, Luoxia Hong made the armillary instrument; afterward Jia Kui, Zhang Heng, and others each had their own, yet in verifying the seven luminaries they all followed the equator.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, Luoxia Hong built an armillary instrument, and later Jia Kui, Zhang Heng, and others each devised their own; yet in computing the seven luminaries they all worked along the equator alone.

sentences.zh: 按冬至極南，夏至極北，而赤道常定于中，國無南北之異。

translations.literal: Now at winter solstice the sun reaches its southern extreme and at summer solstice its northern extreme, while the equator is constantly fixed in the middle, so that the realm has no difference of north and south.
translations.idiomatic: At winter solstice the sun stands farthest south and at summer solstice farthest north, while the equator remains fixed at the center — which is why treating all regions alike along the equator cannot distinguish north from south.

sentences.zh: 蓋渾儀無黃道久矣。

translations.literal: For the armillary instrument has long lacked the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: The armillary instrument had long gone without an ecliptic ring.

sentences.zh: 」太宗異其說，因詔為之。

translations.literal: Taizong marveled at this doctrine and therefore ordered that it be made.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong was struck by this argument and ordered the instrument built.

sentences.zh: 至七年儀成。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the instrument was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the instrument was finished.

sentences.zh: 表裏三重，下據准基，狀如十字，末樹鰲足，以張四表。

translations.literal: It had three layers inside and out; below it rested on a leveling base shaped like a cross, with tortoise feet planted at the ends to spread the four tables.
translations.idiomatic: It had three nested layers; below stood a leveling base in the form of a cross, with tortoise feet at the corners to support the four sighting tables.

sentences.zh: 一曰六合儀，有天經雙規、金渾緯規、金常規，相結於四極之內。

translations.literal: The first was called the Six Harmonies Instrument, with celestial meridian double rings, golden armillary latitude rings, and golden constant rings, joined together within the four poles.
translations.idiomatic: The first was the Six Harmonies Instrument, comprising celestial meridian double rings, golden armillary latitude rings, and golden constant rings, all linked within the four cardinal pivots.

sentences.zh: 列二十八宿、十日、十二辰、經緯三百六十五度。

translations.literal: It marked the twenty-eight lodges, the ten days, the twelve chronograms, and the three hundred sixty-five degrees of longitude and latitude.
translations.idiomatic: It bore the twenty-eight lunar mansions, the ten-day stems, the twelve double-hours, and all three hundred sixty-five degrees of celestial longitude and latitude.

sentences.zh: 二曰三辰儀，圓徑八尺，有璿璣規、月遊規，列宿距度，七曜所行，轉於六合之內。

translations.literal: The second was called the Three Luminaries Instrument, eight feet in circular diameter, with armillary rings and lunar excursion rings, marking lodge intervals and the courses of the seven luminaries, turning within the Six Harmonies.
translations.idiomatic: The second was the Three Luminaries Instrument, eight feet in diameter, fitted with armillary rings and lunar excursion rings that marked the intervals between lodges and the paths of the seven luminaries as they revolved within the Six Harmonies.

sentences.zh: 三曰四游儀，玄樞為軸，以連結玉衡遊筩而貫約矩規。

translations.literal: The third was called the Four Excursions Instrument; the dark pivot served as its axle, linking the jade transverse sighting tube and threading the graduated rings.
translations.idiomatic: The third was the Four Excursions Instrument, with the dark pivot as its axis, joining the jade transverse sighting tube and threading the graduated rings.

sentences.zh: 又玄極北樹北辰，南矩地軸，傍轉於內。

translations.literal: Moreover at the dark pole the northern asterism was planted to the north and the terrestrial axis squared to the south, turning alongside within.
translations.idiomatic: At the dark pole the northern asterism was mounted to the north and the terrestrial axis squared to the south, revolving within the assembly.

sentences.zh: 玉衡在玄樞之間，而南北遊，仰以觀天之辰宿，下以識器之晷度。

translations.literal: The jade transverse lay between the dark pivots and moved north and south; looking up one observed the heavenly lodges, looking down one read the instrument's gnomon degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The jade transverse moved between the dark pivots, traveling north and south: raised, it sighted the celestial mansions; lowered, it read the instrument's graduated shadow scale.

sentences.zh: 皆用銅。

translations.literal: All were made of bronze.
translations.idiomatic: The whole was cast in bronze.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，置於凝暉閣，用之測候。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it and placed it in the Ninghui Pavilion, using it for observation and measurement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and installed it in the Ninghui Pavilion for astronomical observation.

sentences.zh: 閣在禁中，其後遂亡。

translations.literal: The pavilion stood within the inner palace; afterward it was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion stood within the palace precincts; in time the instrument was lost.

sentences.zh: 開元九年，一行受詔，改治新曆，欲知黃道進退，而太史無黃道儀，率府兵曹參軍梁令瓚以木為游儀，一行是之，乃奏：「黃道游儀，古有其術而無其器，昔人潛思，皆未能得。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan, Yixing received an edict to revise the new calendar; wishing to know the advance and retreat of the ecliptic, yet the Grand Astrologer had no ecliptic instrument — the staff officer of the General-in-Chief's office, Liang Lingzan, made a traveling instrument of wood; Yixing approved it and memorialized: "The ecliptic traveling instrument: antiquity had the method but not the device; men of old pondered deeply yet could not obtain it."
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 9, Yixing received orders to reform the calendar. To track the ecliptic's advance and retreat, the Grand Astrologer's office lacked an ecliptic instrument; Staff Officer Liang Lingzan of the General-in-Chief's headquarters built a traveling instrument of wood. Yixing endorsed it and memorialized: "The ecliptic traveling instrument — the ancients knew the method but never possessed the device; thoughtful men of old strove in vain to achieve it."

sentences.zh: 今令瓚所為，日道月交，皆自然契合，于推步尤要，請更鑄以銅鐵。

translations.literal: What Lingzan has now made — the solar path and lunar conjunctions — all fit together naturally; it is especially essential for calendrical computation. I request that it be recast in bronze and iron.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzan's design aligns the solar path and lunar nodes naturally and is indispensable for calendrical calculation. I ask that it be recast in bronze and iron.

sentences.zh: 」十一年儀成。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the instrument was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the instrument was finished.

sentences.zh: 一行又曰：「靈台鐵儀，後魏斛蘭所作，規制樸略，度刻不均，赤道不動，乃如膠柱。

translations.literal: Yixing further said: "The iron instrument of the Spirit Terrace, made by Hulu of Later Wei, was crude in design, its degree marks uneven, and its equator immovable — like tuning pegs glued fast."
translations.idiomatic: Yixing added: "The Spirit Terrace iron instrument made by Hulu of Northern Wei was crude in design, its degree marks uneven, and its equator fixed immovable — like pegs glued to a zither."

sentences.zh: 以考月行，遲速多差，多或至十七度，少不減十度，不足以稽天象、授人時。

translations.literal: Used to examine the moon's motion, its errors in fast and slow were many — sometimes as much as seventeen degrees, never less than ten — insufficient to verify celestial phenomena or grant the seasons to men.
translations.idiomatic: Used to track the moon, its errors in lunar speed were severe — sometimes as much as seventeen degrees, never less than ten — far too crude to verify celestial phenomena or set the seasons for mankind.

sentences.zh: 李淳風黃道儀，以玉衡旋規，別帶日道，傍列二百四十九交，以攜月遊，法頗難，術遂寢廢。

translations.literal: Li Chunfeng's ecliptic instrument used a revolving jade-transverse ring with a separate solar path, listing two hundred forty-nine nodes at the side to carry the moon's excursion — the method was quite difficult, and the technique was eventually abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfeng's ecliptic instrument used a revolving jade-transverse ring with a separate solar track and two hundred forty-nine lunar nodes marked along the side to guide the moon's motion — the method was cumbersome, and the technique fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 臣更造遊儀，使黃道運行，以追列舍之變，因二分之中，以立黃道，交於奎、軫之間，二至陟降，各二十四度。

translations.literal: Your servant has newly made a traveling instrument, causing the ecliptic to move in operation so as to follow changes among the lodges; taking the equinoxes as the mean, the ecliptic is established, crossing between Kui and Zhen; at the two solstices it rises and falls, twenty-four degrees each.
translations.idiomatic: I have devised a new traveling instrument with a movable ecliptic to track shifts among the lunar mansions. Set at the equinoxes, the ecliptic crosses between Kui and Zhen, rising and falling twenty-four degrees at each solstice.

sentences.zh: 黃道內施白道月環，用究陰陽朓，朒，動合天運。

translations.literal: Within the ecliptic a white-path lunar ring is installed, to investigate yin and yang, waxing and waning, its motion matching the celestial cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the ecliptic I have placed a white-path lunar ring to track the moon's waxing and waning, its motion conforming to the heavens.

sentences.zh: 簡而易從，可以制器垂象，永傳不朽。

translations.literal: Simple and easy to follow, it can fashion an instrument and hand down its model, transmitted forever without perishing.
translations.idiomatic: The design is simple and practical — an instrument that can embody the heavens and endure for all time.

sentences.zh: 」於是玄宗嘉之，自為之銘。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Xuanzong praised it and personally composed an inscription for it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong approved and personally composed an inscription for the instrument.

sentences.zh: 又詔一行與令瓚等更鑄渾天銅儀，圓天之象，具列宿赤道及周天度數。

translations.literal: He also ordered Yixing, Lingzan, and others to recast the armillary bronze instrument, the image of the round heaven, fully marking the lodges, equator, and degrees of the entire circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered Yixing, Lingzan, and their colleagues to cast a new armillary bronze instrument depicting the round heaven, complete with the lodges, the equator, and the full circuit of celestial degrees.

sentences.zh: 注水激輪，令其自轉，一晝夜而天運周。

translations.literal: Water was poured in to drive the wheels, causing it to turn of itself; in one day and night the celestial revolution was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Water drove the wheels so that the sphere turned by itself, completing one celestial revolution each day and night.

sentences.zh: 外絡二輪，綴以日月，令得運行。

translations.literal: Two rings were linked on the outside, with sun and moon attached so that they could move in operation.
translations.idiomatic: Two outer rings carried the sun and moon so that they could move along their courses.

sentences.zh: 每天西旋一周，日東行一度，月行十三度十九分度之七，二十九轉有餘而日月會，三百六十五轉而日周天。

translations.literal: Each day the heavens revolved westward one circuit; the sun traveled east one degree; the moon traveled thirteen degrees and seven nineteenths of a degree; after twenty-nine and a fraction of revolutions sun and moon met; after three hundred sixty-five revolutions the sun completed its circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Each day the sky turned westward one full circuit while the sun moved east one degree and the moon thirteen and seven-nineteenth degrees; after twenty-nine-odd revolutions sun and moon converged, and after three hundred sixty-five revolutions the sun completed its annual circuit.

sentences.zh: 以木櫃為地平，令儀半在地下，晦明朔望遲速有准。

translations.literal: A wooden cabinet served as the horizon, so that half the instrument lay below ground; new moon, full moon, and the moon's fast and slow motion all had their standard.
translations.idiomatic: A wooden cabinet formed the horizon, with half the instrument below ground level, so that new moon, full moon, and the moon's varying speed could all be shown accurately.

sentences.zh: 立木人二于地平上：其一前置鼓以候刻，至一刻則自擊之；

translations.literal: Two wooden figures were set on the horizon: one had a drum placed before it to mark the quarters; when a quarter arrived it struck of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Two wooden figures stood on the horizon: one before a drum to mark the quarters of the hour, which it struck automatically when each quarter arrived;

sentences.zh: 其一前置鐘以候辰，至一辰亦自撞之。

translations.literal: the other had a bell placed before it to mark the double-hours; when a double-hour arrived it also struck of itself.
translations.idiomatic: the other before a bell to mark the double-hours, which it likewise struck of itself when each double-hour arrived.

sentences.zh: 皆于櫃中各施輪軸，鉤鍵關鎖，交錯相持。

translations.literal: Within the cabinet wheels and axles were installed for each, with hooks, keys, and locks interlacing to hold one another.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the cabinet, wheels, axles, hooks, and locks meshed together to drive the mechanism.

sentences.zh: 置於武成殿前，以示百官。

translations.literal: It was placed before the Wucheng Hall to display to the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: It was set up before the Wucheng Hall for all the officials to see.

sentences.zh: 無幾而銅鐵漸澀，不能自轉，遂藏於集賢院。

translations.literal: Before long the bronze and iron gradually stiffened and it could no longer turn of itself; it was then stored in the Academy of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the bronze and iron parts seized up and it could no longer turn on its own; it was then stored away in the Academy of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 其黃道遊儀，以古尺四分為度。

translations.literal: Its ecliptic traveling instrument used four fen of the ancient foot per degree.
translations.idiomatic: The ecliptic traveling instrument used four fen of the ancient foot per degree.

sentences.zh: 旋樞雙環，其表一丈四尺六寸一分，縱八分，厚三分，直徑四尺五寸九分，古所謂旋儀也。

translations.literal: The revolving-pivot double ring: its outer surface one zhang, four chi, six cun, and one fen; width eight fen, thickness three fen, diameter four chi, five cun, and nine fen — what antiquity called the revolving instrument.
translations.idiomatic: The revolving-pivot double ring measured one zhang, four chi, six cun, and one fen on its outer face, eight fen wide and three fen thick, with a diameter of four chi, five cun, and nine fen — the instrument the ancients called the revolving sight.

sentences.zh: 南北科兩極，上下循規各三十四度。

translations.literal: North and south were graduated at the two poles; above and below along the rings, thirty-four degrees each.
translations.idiomatic: The north and south poles were graduated, with thirty-four degrees marked above and below along each ring.

sentences.zh: 表裏畫周天度，其一面加之銀釘。

translations.literal: On inside and outside the degrees of the entire circuit were painted; on one face silver pins were added.
translations.idiomatic: The full circuit of degrees was painted on both inner and outer faces, with silver pins set on one side.

sentences.zh: 使東西運轉，如渾天遊旋。

translations.literal: It was made to revolve east and west, like the armillary heaven revolving in excursion.
translations.idiomatic: It could revolve east and west like the turning armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 中旋樞軸，至兩極首內，孔徑大兩度半，長與旋環徑齊。

translations.literal: At the center was the revolving-pivot axle, reaching within the heads of the two poles; bore diameter two and a half degrees, length equal to the revolving ring's diameter.
translations.idiomatic: A central revolving-pivot axle ran to the inner ends of the two poles, with a bore two and a half degrees wide and a length equal to the ring's diameter.

sentences.zh: 玉衡望筩，長四尺五寸八分，廣一寸二分，厚一寸，孔徑六分。

translations.literal: The jade-transverse sighting tube: length four chi, five cun, and eight fen; width one cun and two fen; thickness one cun; bore diameter six fen.
translations.idiomatic: The jade-transverse sighting tube was four chi, five cun, and eight fen long, one cun and two fen wide, one cun thick, with a bore six fen in diameter.

sentences.zh: 衡旋於軸中，旋運持正，用窺七曜及列星之闊狹。

translations.literal: The transverse revolved within the axle, turning while held true, used to sight the seven luminaries and the breadth and narrowness of the arrayed stars.
translations.idiomatic: The transverse revolved on the axle, turning smoothly to sight the seven luminaries and measure the angular separation of the fixed stars.

sentences.zh: 外方內圓，孔徑一度半，周日輪也。

translations.literal: Square outside and round inside, bore diameter one and a half degrees — the solar-day wheel.
translations.idiomatic: Square outside and round inside, with a bore one and a half degrees wide — this was the solar-day wheel.

sentences.zh: 陽經雙環，表一丈七尺三寸，裏一丈四尺六寸四分，廣四寸，厚四分，直徑五尺四寸四分，置於子午。

translations.literal: The solar meridian double ring: outer surface one zhang, seven chi, and three cun; inner one zhang, four chi, six cun, and four fen; width four cun, thickness four fen, diameter five chi, four cun, and four fen — set on the meridian.
translations.idiomatic: The solar meridian double ring had an outer circumference of one zhang, seven chi, and three cun and an inner one of one zhang, four chi, six cun, and four fen; it was four cun wide and four fen thick, with a diameter of five chi, four cun, and four fen, mounted on the meridian.

sentences.zh: 左右用八柱，八柱相固。

translations.literal: To left and right eight pillars were used; the eight pillars were joined firm.
translations.idiomatic: Eight pillars on either side locked the rings firmly in place.

sentences.zh: 亦表裏畫周天度，其一面加之銀釘。

translations.literal: On inside and outside likewise the degrees of the entire circuit were painted; on one face silver pins were added.
translations.idiomatic: The full circuit of degrees was likewise painted on both faces, with silver pins on one side.

sentences.zh: 半出地上，半入地下。

translations.literal: Half emerged above ground, half entered below ground.
translations.idiomatic: Half stood above the horizon and half below.

sentences.zh: 雙間挾樞軸及玉衡望筩旋環於中也。

translations.literal: The double gap clasped the pivot axle and the jade-transverse sighting tube's revolving ring in the center.
translations.idiomatic: The gap between the rings enclosed the pivot axle and the jade-transverse sighting tube at the center.

sentences.zh: 陰緯單環，外內廣厚周徑，皆准陽經，與陽經相銜各半，內外俱齊。

translations.literal: The lunar latitude single ring: outer and inner width, thickness, and circumference all matched the solar meridian; it interlocked with the solar meridian half and half, inner and outer both flush.
translations.idiomatic: The lunar latitude single ring matched the solar meridian ring in width, thickness, and circumference, interlocking with it half and half so that inner and outer edges aligned perfectly.

sentences.zh: 面平，上為天，下為地。

translations.literal: The face was level; above was Heaven, below was Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Its face was level — above was heaven, below was earth.

sentences.zh: 橫周陽環，謂之陰渾也。

translations.literal: It crossed horizontally around the solar ring — called the lunar armillary.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing horizontally around the solar ring, it was called the lunar armillary.

sentences.zh: 平上為兩界，內外為周天百刻。

translations.literal: On the level above were two boundaries; inside and outside were the hundred quarters of the entire circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The level upper face bore two boundaries marking the hundred quarters of the full celestial circuit inside and out.

sentences.zh: 天頂單環，表一丈七尺三寸，縱廣八尺，厚三分，直徑五尺四寸四分。

translations.literal: The celestial summit single ring: outer surface one zhang, seven chi, and three cun; length and breadth eight chi; thickness three fen; diameter five chi, four cun, and four fen.
translations.idiomatic: The celestial summit single ring measured one zhang, seven chi, and three cun around its outer face, eight chi long and wide, three fen thick, with a diameter of five chi, four cun, and four fen.

sentences.zh: 直中國人頂之上，東西當卯酉之中，稍南，使見日出入。

translations.literal: It stood straight above the crown of a man of China; east and west aligned with the middle of mao and you; slightly to the south, so that one might see the sun's rising and setting.
translations.idiomatic: It stood directly above the observer's head, aligned east-west between mao and you, tilted slightly south so that sunrise and sunset could be observed.

sentences.zh: 令與陽經、陰緯相固，如鳥殼之裹黃。

translations.literal: It was made to join firm with the solar meridian and lunar latitude, like a shell enclosing the yolk.
translations.idiomatic: It was locked to the solar meridian and lunar latitude rings like a shell enclosing its yolk.

sentences.zh: 南去赤道三十六度，去黃道十二度，去北極五十五度，去南北平各九十一度強。

translations.literal: South it stood thirty-six degrees from the equator, twelve degrees from the ecliptic, fifty-five degrees from the north pole, and from the north-south level ninety-one and a fraction degrees each.
translations.idiomatic: It stood thirty-six degrees south of the equator, twelve degrees from the ecliptic, fifty-five degrees from the north pole, and ninety-one-odd degrees from each horizontal plane.

sentences.zh: 赤道單環，表一丈四尺五寸九分，橫八分，厚三分，直徑四尺五寸八分。

translations.literal: The equator single ring: outer surface one zhang, four chi, five cun, and nine fen; width eight fen crosswise, thickness three fen, diameter four chi, five cun, and eight fen.
translations.idiomatic: The equator single ring measured one zhang, four chi, five cun, and nine fen around its outer face, eight fen wide and three fen thick, with a diameter of four chi, five cun, and eight fen.

sentences.zh: 赤道者，當天之中，二十八宿之位也。

translations.literal: The equator is at the center of Heaven — the position of the twenty-eight lodges.
translations.idiomatic: The equator marks the center of heaven — the station of the twenty-eight lunar mansions.

sentences.zh: 雙規運動，度穿一穴。

translations.literal: The double rings moved in operation; one degree pierced a hole.
translations.idiomatic: The double rings could move, with a hole pierced at each degree.

sentences.zh: 古者，秋分日在角五度，今在軫十三度；

translations.literal: In antiquity, at the autumn equinox the sun stood at five degrees of Jiao; now it is at thirteen degrees of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the autumn equinox sun stood at five degrees of Jiao; now it stands at thirteen degrees of Zhen;

sentences.zh: 冬至日在牽牛初，今在斗十度。

translations.literal: at the winter solstice the sun stood at the beginning of Qianniu; now it is at ten degrees of Dou.
translations.idiomatic: at the winter solstice it stood at the beginning of Qianniu, but now at ten degrees of Dou.

sentences.zh: 隨穴退交，不復差繆。

translations.literal: Following the hole it retreats at the crossing, no longer erring.
translations.idiomatic: By shifting the hole at each crossing, the instrument no longer drifts out of alignment.

sentences.zh: 傍在卯酉之南，上去天頂三十六度，而橫置之。

translations.literal: It lay to the south of mao and you; above, thirty-six degrees from the celestial summit, and was set horizontally.
translations.idiomatic: It lay south of mao and you, thirty-six degrees below the celestial summit, mounted horizontally.

sentences.zh: 黃道單環，表一丈五尺四寸一分，橫八分，厚四分，直徑四尺八寸四分。

translations.literal: The ecliptic single ring: outer surface one zhang, five chi, four cun, and one fen; width eight fen crosswise, thickness four fen, diameter four chi, eight cun, and four fen.
translations.idiomatic: The ecliptic single ring measured one zhang, five chi, four cun, and one fen around its outer face, eight fen wide and four fen thick, with a diameter of four chi, eight cun, and four fen.

sentences.zh: 日之所行，故名橫道。

translations.literal: Where the sun travels — hence called the transverse path.
translations.idiomatic: It marks the sun's path and is therefore called the transverse track.

sentences.zh: 太陽陟降，積歲有差。

translations.literal: The great sun's rising and falling accumulates discrepancies over the years.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's north-south shift accumulates error over the years.

sentences.zh: 月及五星，亦隨日度出入。

translations.literal: The moon and the five stars likewise follow the sun's degrees in entering and emerging.
translations.idiomatic: The moon and the five planets likewise enter and leave along the sun's degrees.

sentences.zh: 古無其器，規制不知准的，斟酌為率，疏闊尤甚。

translations.literal: Antiquity had no such instrument; its design and standard were unknown, and estimates used as ratios were especially coarse and wide.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity had no such instrument; without a standard design, calendrical estimates were especially crude.

sentences.zh: 今設此環，置於赤道環內，仍開合使運轉，出入四十八度，而極畫兩方，東西列周天度數，南北列百刻，可使見日知時。

translations.literal: Now this ring is installed within the equator ring, still opening and closing so that it may turn in operation, entering and emerging forty-eight degrees; at the poles two sides are painted, east and west listing the degrees of the entire circuit, north and south listing the hundred quarters — so that one may see the sun and know the time.
translations.idiomatic: This ring is now set inside the equator ring, hinged so it can rotate through forty-eight degrees. The poles are marked on both sides — degrees of the full circuit east and west, the hundred time-quarters north and south — so that one can observe the sun and tell the hour.

sentences.zh: 上列三百六十策，與用卦相准。

translations.literal: Above are listed three hundred sixty counting rods, matching the hexagrams in use.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred sixty counting rods are marked above, aligned with the hexagrams used in calculation.

sentences.zh: 度穿一穴，與赤道相交。

translations.literal: Each degree pierces a hole, intersecting the equator.
translations.idiomatic: A hole is pierced at each degree where the ring crosses the equator.

sentences.zh: 白道月環，表一丈五尺一寸五分，橫八分，厚三分，直徑四尺七寸六分。

translations.literal: The white-path lunar ring: outer surface one zhang, five chi, one cun, and five fen; width eight fen crosswise, thickness three fen, diameter four chi, seven cun, and six fen.
translations.idiomatic: The white-path lunar ring measured one zhang, five chi, one cun, and five fen around its outer face, eight fen wide and three fen thick, with a diameter of four chi, seven cun, and six fen.

sentences.zh: 用行有迂曲遲速，與日行緩急相及。

translations.literal: Its motion has winding, slow, and fast phases, matching the sun's daily easing and hastening.
translations.idiomatic: The moon's winding course and varying speed are matched against the sun's daily motion.

sentences.zh: 古亦無其器，今設于黃道環內，使就黃道為交合，出入六度，以測每夜月離，上畫周天度數，度穿一穴，擬移交會。

translations.literal: Antiquity likewise had no such instrument; now it is set within the ecliptic ring, made to join the ecliptic in conjunction, entering and emerging six degrees, to measure each night's lunar separation; above the degrees of the entire circuit are painted, each degree piercing a hole, approximating the shifting nodes of conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity had no such instrument either; it is now set inside the ecliptic ring, joining the ecliptic at conjunction and moving through six degrees to measure the moon's nightly separation. The full circuit of degrees is painted above, with a hole at each degree to track the shifting nodes.

sentences.zh: 皆用鋼鐵。

translations.literal: All were made of steel and iron.
translations.idiomatic: All were cast in steel and iron.

sentences.zh: 游儀，四柱為龍，其崇四尺七寸，水槽及山崇一尺七寸半，槽長六尺九寸，高、廣皆四寸，池深一寸，廣一寸半。

translations.literal: The traveling instrument: four pillars shaped as dragons, their height four chi and seven cun; the water trough and mountain height one chi, seven cun, and a half; trough length six chi and nine cun, height and breadth each four cun; pool depth one cun, breadth one cun and a half.
translations.idiomatic: The traveling instrument stood on four dragon pillars four chi and seven cun high. The water trough and its mountain ornament rose one chi, seven cun, and a half; the trough was six chi and nine cun long, four cun high and wide, with a pool one cun deep and one cun and a half wide.

sentences.zh: 龍能興雲雨，故以飾柱。

translations.literal: Dragons can raise clouds and rain — hence they adorn the pillars.
translations.idiomatic: Dragons were chosen to adorn the pillars because they summon clouds and rain.

sentences.zh: 柱在四維。

translations.literal: The pillars stood at the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: The pillars stood at the four diagonal corners.

sentences.zh: 龍下有山、雲，俱在水準槽上。

translations.literal: Below the dragons were mountains and clouds, all upon the leveling trough.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and clouds were set below the dragons on the leveling trough.

sentences.zh: 皆用銅。

translations.literal: All were made of bronze.
translations.idiomatic: These parts were all cast in bronze.

sentences.zh: 其所測宿度與古異者：舊經，角距星去極九十一度，亢八十九度，氐九十四度，房百八度，心百八度，尾百二十度，箕百一十八度，南斗百一十六度，牽牛百六度，須女百度，虛百四度，危九十七度，營室八十五度，東壁八十六度，奎七十六度，婁八十度，胃、昴七十四度，畢七十八度，觜觿、八十四度，參九十四度，東井七十度，輿鬼六十八度，柳七十七度，七星九十一度，張九十七度，翼九十七度，軫九十八度。

translations.literal: Among the lodge degrees they measured that differ from antiquity: the old canon had the Horn pivot star at ninety-one degrees from the pole, Neck at eighty-nine degrees, Root at ninety-four degrees, Room at one hundred eight degrees, Heart at one hundred eight degrees, Tail at one hundred twenty degrees, Winnowing Basket at one hundred eighteen degrees, Southern Dipper at one hundred sixteen degrees, Ox Leader at one hundred six degrees, Maid at one hundred degrees, Emptiness at one hundred four degrees, Rooftop at ninety-seven degrees, Encampment at eighty-five degrees, Eastern Wall at eighty-six degrees, Strider at seventy-six degrees, Bond at eighty degrees, Stomach and Hairy Head at seventy-four degrees, Net at seventy-eight degrees, Turtle Beak at eighty-four degrees, Three Stars at ninety-four degrees, Well at seventy degrees, Chariot Ghost at sixty-eight degrees, Willow at seventy-seven degrees, Seven Stars at ninety-one degrees, Extended Net at ninety-seven degrees, Wings at ninety-seven degrees, and Axletree at ninety-eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The measured lodge degrees that differ from the old records are as follows. In the old canon, the Horn pivot star stood ninety-one degrees from the pole; Neck, eighty-nine; Root, ninety-four; Room, one hundred eight; Heart, one hundred eight; Tail, one hundred twenty; Winnowing Basket, one hundred eighteen; Southern Dipper, one hundred sixteen; Ox Leader, one hundred six; Maid, one hundred; Emptiness, one hundred four; Rooftop, ninety-seven; Encampment, eighty-five; Eastern Wall, eighty-six; Strider, seventy-six; Bond, eighty; Stomach and Hairy Head, seventy-four; Net, seventy-eight; Turtle Beak, eighty-four; Three Stars, ninety-four; Well, seventy; Chariot Ghost, sixty-eight; Willow, seventy-seven; Seven Stars, ninety-one; Extended Net, ninety-seven; Wings, ninety-seven; and Axletree, ninety-eight.

sentences.zh: 今測，角九十三度半，亢九十一度半，氐九十八度，房百一十度半，心百一十度，尾百二十四度，箕百二十度，南斗百一十九度，牽牛百四度，須女百一度，虛百一度，危九十七度，營室八十三度，東壁八十四度，奎七十三度，婁七十七度，胃、昴七十二度，畢七十六度，觜觿八十二度，參九十三度，東井六十八度，輿鬼六十八度，柳八十度半，七星九十三度半，張百度，翼百三度，軫百度。

translations.literal: Now measured: Horn ninety-three and a half degrees, Neck ninety-one and a half degrees, Root ninety-eight degrees, Room one hundred ten and a half degrees, Heart one hundred ten degrees, Tail one hundred twenty-four degrees, Winnowing Basket one hundred twenty degrees, Southern Dipper one hundred nineteen degrees, Ox Leader one hundred four degrees, Maid one hundred one degrees, Emptiness one hundred one degrees, Rooftop ninety-seven degrees, Encampment eighty-three degrees, Eastern Wall eighty-four degrees, Strider seventy-three degrees, Bond seventy-seven degrees, Stomach and Hairy Head seventy-two degrees, Net seventy-six degrees, Turtle Beak eighty-two degrees, Three Stars ninety-three degrees, Well sixty-eight degrees, Chariot Ghost sixty-eight degrees, Willow eighty and a half degrees, Seven Stars ninety-three and a half degrees, Extended Net one hundred degrees, Wings one hundred three degrees, Axletree one hundred degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The new measurements give Horn at ninety-three and a half degrees; Neck, ninety-one and a half; Root, ninety-eight; Room, one hundred ten and a half; Heart, one hundred ten; Tail, one hundred twenty-four; Winnowing Basket, one hundred twenty; Southern Dipper, one hundred nineteen; Ox Leader, one hundred four; Maid, one hundred one; Emptiness, one hundred one; Rooftop, ninety-seven; Encampment, eighty-three; Eastern Wall, eighty-four; Strider, seventy-three; Bond, seventy-seven; Stomach and Hairy Head, seventy-two; Net, seventy-six; Turtle Beak, eighty-two; Three Stars, ninety-three; Well, sixty-eight; Chariot Ghost, sixty-eight; Willow, eighty and a half; Seven Stars, ninety-three and a half; Extended Net, one hundred; Wings, one hundred three; and Axletree, one hundred.

sentences.zh: 又舊經，角距星正當赤道，黃道在其南；

translations.literal: Again, in the old canon the Horn pivot star stood directly on the equator, and the ecliptic lay south of it;
translations.idiomatic: In the old canon, moreover, the Horn pivot star lay directly on the equator, with the ecliptic to its south;

sentences.zh: 今測，角在赤道南二度半，則黃道復經角中，與天象合。

translations.literal: now measured, Horn is two and a half degrees south of the equator, so the ecliptic again passes through the middle of Horn, matching the celestial appearance.
translations.idiomatic: the new measurement places Horn two and a half degrees south of the equator, so that the ecliptic once again runs through the middle of the lodge — in agreement with the sky.

sentences.zh: 虛北星舊圖入虛，今測在須女九度。

translations.literal: The northern star of Emptiness in the old chart entered Emptiness; now measured, it is at nine degrees of Maid.
translations.idiomatic: The northern star of Emptiness was placed within Emptiness on the old chart; it is now measured at nine degrees of Maid.

sentences.zh: 危北星舊圖入危，今測在虛六度半。

translations.literal: The northern star of Rooftop in the old chart entered Rooftop; now measured, it is at six and a half degrees of Emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: The northern star of Rooftop was placed within Rooftop on the old chart; it is now measured at six and a half degrees of Emptiness.

sentences.zh: 又奎誤距以西大星，故壁損二度，奎增二度；

translations.literal: Again, Strider wrongly took the western great star as pivot, so Eastern Wall lost two degrees and Strider gained two degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Strider had also been wrongly measured from the western great star, reducing Eastern Wall by two degrees and inflating Strider by two;

sentences.zh: 今復距西南大星，即奎、壁各得本度。

translations.literal: now again taking the southwest great star as pivot, Strider and Eastern Wall each recover their proper degrees.
translations.idiomatic: measuring again from the southwest great star restores the proper degree allotments for Strider and Eastern Wall.

sentences.zh: 畢、赤道十六度，黃道亦十六度。

translations.literal: Net: sixteen degrees on the equator, and likewise sixteen degrees on the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: Net was given sixteen degrees on the equator and sixteen on the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 觜觿，赤道二度，黃道三度。

translations.literal: Turtle Beak: two degrees on the equator, three degrees on the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: Turtle Beak was given two degrees on the equator and three on the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 二宿俱當黃道斜虛，畢尚與赤道度同，觜觿總二度，黃道損加一度，蓋其誤也。

translations.literal: Both lodges lay where the ecliptic slants across open space; Net still matched the equatorial degrees, but Turtle Beak totaled two degrees while the ecliptic was increased by one degree — this was surely the error.
translations.idiomatic: Both lodges lie where the ecliptic cuts obliquely across the sky. Net still matched its equatorial span, but Turtle Beak totaled only two degrees while the ecliptic figure had been inflated by one — clearly an error.

sentences.zh: 今測畢十七度半，觜觿半度。

translations.literal: Now measured: Net seventeen and a half degrees, Turtle Beak half a degree.
translations.idiomatic: The new measurements give Net seventeen and a half degrees and Turtle Beak half a degree.

sentences.zh: 又柳誤距以第四星，今復用第三星。

translations.literal: Again, Willow wrongly took the fourth star as pivot; now the third star is used again.
translations.idiomatic: Willow had also been wrongly measured from the fourth star; the third star is now restored as pivot.

sentences.zh: 張中央四星為硃鳥嗉，外二星為翼，北距以翼而不距以膺，故張增二度半，七星減二度半；

translations.literal: The four central stars of Extended Net are the Vermillion Bird's crop; the two outer stars are the wings. The northern pivot was taken from the wings rather than the breast, so Extended Net gained two and a half degrees and Seven Stars lost two and a half degrees;
translations.idiomatic: The four central stars of Extended Net form the Vermillion Bird's crop, with the two outer stars as its wings. Because the northern pivot was taken from the wings rather than the breast, Extended Net was inflated by two and a half degrees and Seven Stars reduced by two and a half;

sentences.zh: 今復以膺為距，則七星、張各得本度。

translations.literal: now again taking the breast as pivot, Seven Stars and Extended Net each recover their proper degrees.
translations.idiomatic: measuring again from the breast restores the proper degrees for Seven Stars and Extended Net.

sentences.zh: 其他星：舊經，文昌二星在輿鬼，四星在東井。

translations.literal: Other stars: in the old canon, two stars of Wenchang were in Chariot Ghost and four stars in Well.
translations.idiomatic: Other stars: in the old canon, two stars of Wenchang lay in Chariot Ghost and four in Well.

sentences.zh: 北斗樞在七星一度，璿在張二度，機在翼二度，權在翼八度，衡在軫八度，開陽在角七度，杓在亢四度。

translations.literal: The Northern Dipper's Pivot was at one degree of Seven Stars, Xuan at two degrees of Extended Net, Ji at two degrees of Wings, Quan at eight degrees of Wings, Heng at eight degrees of Axletree, Kaiyang at seven degrees of Horn, and the Ladle at four degrees of Neck.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Dipper's Pivot stood at one degree of Seven Stars; Xuan, at two degrees of Extended Net; Ji, at two degrees of Wings; Quan, at eight degrees of Wings; Heng, at eight degrees of Axletree; Kaiyang, at seven degrees of Horn; and the Ladle, at four degrees of Neck.

sentences.zh: 天關在黃道南四度，天尊、天槨在黃道北，天江、天高、狗國、外屏、雲雨、虛梁在黃道外，天囷、土公吏在赤道外，上臺在東井，中台在七星，建星在黃道北半度，天苑在昴、畢，王良在壁，外屏在觜觿，雷電在赤道外五度，霹靂在赤道外四度，八魁在營室，長垣、羅堰當黃道。

translations.literal: Heaven's Gate was four degrees south of the ecliptic; Heaven's Honor and Heaven's Coffin were north of the ecliptic; Heaven's River, Heaven's Height, Dog Country, Outer Screen, Cloud and Rain, and Empty Bridge were outside the ecliptic; Heaven's Granary and Earth Duke's Clerk were outside the equator; Upper Terrace was in Well, Middle Terrace in Seven Stars, Establishment Stars half a degree north of the ecliptic, Heaven's Park in Hairy Head and Net, Wangliang in Wall, Outer Screen in Turtle Beak, Thunder and Lightning five degrees outside the equator, Thunderclap four degrees outside the equator, Eight Chiefs in Encampment, Long Rampart and Net Weir on the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Gate lay four degrees south of the ecliptic; Heaven's Honor and Heaven's Coffin, north of it. Heaven's River, Heaven's Height, Dog Country, Outer Screen, Cloud and Rain, and Empty Bridge stood outside the ecliptic; Heaven's Granary and Earth Duke's Clerk, outside the equator. Upper Terrace was in Well; Middle Terrace, in Seven Stars; Establishment Stars, half a degree north of the ecliptic; Heaven's Park, in Hairy Head and Net; Wangliang, in Wall; Outer Screen, in Turtle Beak; Thunder and Lightning, five degrees outside the equator; Thunderclap, four degrees outside the equator; Eight Chiefs, in Encampment; and Long Rampart and Net Weir, on the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 今測，文昌四星在柳，一星在輿鬼，一星在東井。

translations.literal: Now measured: four stars of Wenchang are in Willow, one star in Chariot Ghost, and one star in Well.
translations.idiomatic: The new measurements place four stars of Wenchang in Willow, one in Chariot Ghost, and one in Well.

sentences.zh: 北斗樞在張十三度，璿在張十二度半，機在翼十三度，權在翼十七度太，衡在軫十度半，開陽在角四度少，杓在角十二度少。

translations.literal: The Northern Dipper's Pivot is at thirteen degrees of Extended Net, Xuan at twelve and a half degrees of Extended Net, Ji at thirteen degrees of Wings, Quan at seventeen and excess degrees of Wings, Heng at ten and a half degrees of Axletree, Kaiyang at four and deficit degrees of Horn, and the Ladle at twelve and deficit degrees of Horn.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Dipper's Pivot now stands at thirteen degrees of Extended Net; Xuan, at twelve and a half degrees of Extended Net; Ji, at thirteen degrees of Wings; Quan, at slightly more than seventeen degrees of Wings; Heng, at ten and a half degrees of Axletree; Kaiyang, at slightly less than four degrees of Horn; and the Ladle, at slightly less than twelve degrees of Horn.

sentences.zh: 天關、天尊、天槨、天江、天高、狗國、外屏，皆當黃道。

translations.literal: Heaven's Gate, Heaven's Honor, Heaven's Coffin, Heaven's River, Heaven's Height, Dog Country, and Outer Screen all lie on the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Gate, Heaven's Honor, Heaven's Coffin, Heaven's River, Heaven's Height, Dog Country, and Outer Screen all lie on the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 雲雨在黃道內七度，虛梁在黃道內四度，天囷當赤道，土公吏在赤道內六度，上臺在柳，中台在張，建星在黃道北四度半，天苑在胃、昴，王良四星在奎，一星在壁，外屏在畢，雷電在赤道內二度，霹靂四星在赤道內，一星在外，八魁五星在壁，四星在營室，長垣在黃道北五度，羅堰在黃道北。

translations.literal: Cloud and Rain is seven degrees inside the ecliptic, Empty Bridge four degrees inside the ecliptic, Heaven's Granary on the equator, Earth Duke's Clerk six degrees inside the equator, Upper Terrace in Willow, Middle Terrace in Extended Net, Establishment Stars four and a half degrees north of the ecliptic, Heaven's Park in Stomach and Hairy Head, four stars of Wangliang in Strider and one star in Wall, Outer Screen in Net, Thunder and Lightning two degrees inside the equator, four stars of Thunderclap inside the equator and one star outside, five stars of Eight Chiefs in Wall and four stars in Encampment, Long Rampart five degrees north of the ecliptic, and Net Weir north of the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud and Rain lies seven degrees inside the ecliptic; Empty Bridge, four degrees inside; Heaven's Granary, on the equator; Earth Duke's Clerk, six degrees inside the equator. Upper Terrace is in Willow; Middle Terrace, in Extended Net; Establishment Stars, four and a half degrees north of the ecliptic; Heaven's Park, in Stomach and Hairy Head. Four stars of Wangliang lie in Strider and one in Wall; Outer Screen, in Net; Thunder and Lightning, two degrees inside the equator. Four stars of Thunderclap lie inside the equator and one outside. Five stars of Eight Chiefs lie in Wall and four in Encampment. Long Rampart stands five degrees north of the ecliptic, and Net Weir, north of the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 黃道，春分與赤道交於奎五度太；

translations.literal: On the ecliptic, the spring equinox intersects the equator at five and excess degrees of Strider;
translations.idiomatic: On the ecliptic, the spring equinox crosses the equator at slightly more than five degrees of Strider;

sentences.zh: 秋分交於軫十四度少；

translations.literal: the autumn equinox intersects at fourteen and deficit degrees of Axletree;
translations.idiomatic: the autumn equinox, at slightly less than fourteen degrees of Axletree;

sentences.zh: 冬至在斗十度，去赤道南二十四度；

translations.literal: the winter solstice is at ten degrees of Dipper, twenty-four degrees south of the equator;
translations.idiomatic: the winter solstice at ten degrees of Dipper, twenty-four degrees south of the equator;

sentences.zh: 夏至在井十三度少，去赤道北二十四度。

translations.literal: the summer solstice is at thirteen and deficit degrees of Well, twenty-four degrees north of the equator.
translations.idiomatic: and the summer solstice at slightly less than thirteen degrees of Well, twenty-four degrees north of the equator.

sentences.zh: 其赤道帶天之中，以分列宿之度。

translations.literal: The equator girds the center of Heaven, by which the degrees of the lodges are apportioned.
translations.idiomatic: The equator girdles the center of heaven and serves to divide the degrees among the lodges.

sentences.zh: 黃道斜運，以明日月之行。

translations.literal: The ecliptic runs obliquely, to clarify the motion of the sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: The ecliptic runs obliquely to mark the paths of the sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 乃立八節、九限，校二道差數，著之歷經。

translations.literal: Then the eight seasonal nodes and nine limits were established, the discrepancy numbers of the two paths were checked, and they were recorded in the calendrical canon.
translations.idiomatic: The eight seasonal nodes and nine limits were then established, the discrepancies between the two paths calculated, and the results entered in the calendrical canon.

sentences.zh: 蓋天之說，李淳風以為天地中高而四頹，日月相隱蔽，以為晝夜。

translations.literal: In the hemispherical-dome theory, Li Chunfeng held that Heaven and Earth are high at the center and slope down on all four sides; sun and moon conceal and reveal each other, making day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In the hemispherical-dome theory, Li Chunfeng held that heaven and earth rise high at the center and slope away on all sides, and that the sun and moon alternately conceal and reveal each other to produce day and night.

sentences.zh: 繞北極常見者謂之上規，南極常隱者謂之下規，赤道橫絡者謂之中規。

translations.literal: What constantly circles the north pole and remains visible is called the upper gnomon; what constantly circles the south pole and remains hidden is called the lower gnomon; what the equator crosses horizontally is called the middle gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: The region that constantly circles the north pole and stays visible is called the upper gnomon; that which circles the south pole and stays hidden, the lower gnomon; and the equator's horizontal belt, the middle gnomon.

sentences.zh: 及一行考月行出入黃道，為圖三十六，究九道之增損，而蓋天之狀見矣。

translations.literal: When Yixing examined the moon's entering and emerging from the ecliptic, he made thirty-six diagrams, investigating the increase and decrease of the nine paths, and the form of the hemispherical dome became visible.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixing studied the moon's entry into and departure from the ecliptic, he drew thirty-six diagrams tracing the variations of the nine lunar paths, and the shape of the hemispherical dome took form.

sentences.zh: 削篾為度，徑一分，其厚半之，長與圖等，穴其正中，植針為樞，令可環運。

translations.literal: Bamboo splints were cut for degree measures: diameter one fen, thickness half that, length equal to the diagram; a hole was bored at the center, a needle planted as pivot, so that it could revolve in a circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo splints were cut to serve as degree measures — one fen in diameter, half that in thickness, and as long as the diagram. A hole was bored at the center, a needle set as pivot, and the splint made to revolve freely.

sentences.zh: 自中樞之外，均刻百四十七度。

translations.literal: Outward from the central pivot, one hundred forty-seven degrees were evenly marked.
translations.idiomatic: Outward from the central pivot, one hundred forty-seven degrees were evenly marked.

sentences.zh: 全度之末，旋為外規。

translations.literal: At the end of the full degrees, it was bent into the outer gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the full degree span, the splint was bent to form the outer gnomon.

sentences.zh: 規外太半度，再旋為重規。

translations.literal: Beyond the gnomon by slightly more than half a degree, it was bent again into a double gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: Slightly more than half a degree beyond that, it was bent again to form a second gnomon.

sentences.zh: 以均賦周天度分。

translations.literal: The degrees and parts of the entire circuit were evenly allotted.
translations.idiomatic: The degrees and fractional parts of the full circuit were evenly distributed across it.

sentences.zh: 又距極樞九十一度少半，旋為赤道帶天之紘。

translations.literal: Again, at ninety-one and a little less than half degrees from the polar pivot, it was bent into the equator girdling Heaven's circumference.
translations.idiomatic: At ninety-one and a fraction degrees from the polar pivot, it was bent again to form the equator girdling heaven's circumference.

sentences.zh: 距極三十五度旋為內規。

translations.literal: At thirty-five degrees from the pole it was bent into the inner gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty-five degrees from the pole, it was bent to form the inner gnomon.

sentences.zh: 乃步冬至日躔所在，以正辰次之中，以立宿距。

translations.literal: Then the winter solstice sun's station was paced to fix the center of the chronogram sequence and establish lodge pivots.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's position at the winter solstice was then stepped off to fix the center of the chronogram sequence and establish the lodge pivots.

sentences.zh: 按渾儀所測，甘、石、巫鹹眾星明者，皆以篾，橫考入宿距，縱考去極度，而後圖之。

translations.literal: According to measurements by the armillary sphere, all the bright stars of Gan, Shi, and Wu were placed with splints, horizontally checked into lodge pivots, vertically checked for degrees from the pole, and then plotted on the diagram.
translations.idiomatic: Using the armillary sphere's measurements, all bright stars from the Gan, Shi, and Wu star catalogs were placed with splints — checked horizontally against lodge pivots and vertically for polar distance — and then plotted on the diagram.

sentences.zh: 其赤道外眾星疏密之狀，與仰視小殊者，由渾儀去南極漸近，其度益狹；

translations.literal: The density and sparsity of stars outside the equator differ slightly from direct observation because, on the armillary sphere, as one approaches the south pole the degrees grow ever narrower;
translations.idiomatic: The spacing of stars outside the equator differs slightly from what one sees looking up because on the armillary sphere, as one approaches the south pole, the degrees grow progressively narrower;

sentences.zh: 而蓋圖漸遠，其度益廣使然。

translations.literal: whereas on the hemispherical diagram, as one moves farther away, the degrees grow ever wider — hence the difference.
translations.idiomatic: whereas on the hemispherical diagram, farther from the center the degrees grow progressively wider — hence the discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 若考其去極入宿度數，移之於渾天則一也。

translations.literal: If one checks their degrees from the pole and entry into lodges and transfers them to the armillary heaven, they are one and the same.
translations.idiomatic: But if one checks their polar distances and lodge positions and transfers them to the armillary sphere, the two agree.

sentences.zh: 又赤道內外，其廣狹不均，若就二至出入赤道二十四度，以規度之，則二分所交不得其正；

translations.literal: Again, inside and outside the equator the breadth and narrowness are uneven; if one measures by the solstices' twenty-four degrees of entry and emergence from the equator, the equinox crossings cannot be placed correctly;
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the equator, moreover, the widths are uneven. If one measures from the solstices' twenty-four degrees of departure from the equator, the equinox crossings cannot be placed correctly;

sentences.zh: 自二分黃赤道交，以規度之，則二至距極度數不得其正；

translations.literal: if one measures from the equinox crossings of ecliptic and equator, the solstice degrees from the pole cannot be placed correctly;
translations.idiomatic: if one measures from the equinox crossings of the ecliptic and equator, the solstice polar distances cannot be placed correctly;

sentences.zh: 當求赤道分、至之中，均刻為七十二限，據每黃道差數，以篾度量而識之，然後規為黃道，則周天鹹得其正矣。

translations.literal: one should seek the midpoints between equinox and solstice on the equator, evenly mark seventy-two limits, and according to each ecliptic discrepancy number measure and mark them with splints; then bend the ecliptic — and the entire circuit will all be correct.
translations.idiomatic: one must find the midpoints between equinox and solstice on the equator, divide them evenly into seventy-two limits, and mark each ecliptic discrepancy with a splint measure. Only then, by bending the ecliptic, will the full circuit be correct throughout.

sentences.zh: 又考黃道二分二至之中，均刻為七十二候，定陰陽曆二交所在，依月去黃道度，率差一候，亦以篾度量而識之，然後規為月道，則周天鹹得其正矣。

translations.literal: Again, examining the midpoints between the ecliptic's two equinoxes and two solstices, evenly mark seventy-two hou, fix the positions of the two nodes in the yin-yang calendar, and according to the moon's degrees from the ecliptic, for each hou of discrepancy likewise measure and mark with splints; then bend the lunar path — and the entire circuit will all be correct.
translations.idiomatic: Similarly, the midpoints between the ecliptic's two equinoxes and two solstices should be divided evenly into seventy-two hou, the positions of the two lunar nodes fixed, and for each hou of discrepancy in the moon's distance from the ecliptic, a splint measure applied. Only then, by bending the lunar path, will the full circuit be correct throughout.

sentences.zh: 中晷之法。

translations.literal: The method of the noon gnomon shadow.
translations.idiomatic: The method of the noon gnomon shadow.

sentences.zh: 初，淳風造曆，定二十四氣中晷，與祖沖之短長頗異，然未知其孰是。

translations.literal: At first, when Chunfeng made his calendar, he fixed the noon gnomon shadows of the twenty-four qi, which differed considerably from Zu Chongzhi's lengths and shorts, yet it was not known which was correct.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chunfeng first compiled his calendar, he fixed the noon gnomon shadows for the twenty-four qi — figures that differed considerably from Zu Chongzhi's — but which was correct remained unknown.

sentences.zh: 及一行作《大衍曆》，詔太史測天下之晷，求其土中，以為定數。

translations.literal: When Yixing compiled the Dayan Calendar, an edict ordered the Grand Clerk to measure gnomon shadows throughout the realm, seek its terrestrial center, and use that as the fixed standard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixing compiled the Dayan Calendar, an edict ordered the Grand Clerk to measure gnomon shadows across the empire, determine the terrestrial center, and establish fixed constants from the results.

sentences.zh: 其議曰：

translations.literal: The discussion states:
translations.idiomatic: The memorial argued as follows:

sentences.zh: 《周禮·大司徒》：「以土圭之法測土深。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou, Grand Minister of Education: "By the method of the earth square, measure the depth of the earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, Grand Minister of Education: "By the method of the earth square, measure the depth of the earth.

sentences.zh: 日至之景，尺有五寸，謂之地中。

translations.literal: The shadow at the sun's arrival is one chi and five cun — this is called the terrestrial center.
translations.idiomatic: Where the solstice shadow measures one chi and five cun, that is called the terrestrial center.

sentences.zh: 」鄭氏以為「日景於地，千里而差一寸。

translations.literal: " Zheng's commentary holds that "the sun's shadow on earth differs one cun for each thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng's commentary explains: "The sun's shadow on earth differs by one cun for each thousand li.

sentences.zh: 尺有五寸者，南戴日下萬五千里，地與星辰四游升降於三萬里內，是以半之，得地中，今潁川陽城是也」。

translations.literal: One chi and five cun means fifteen thousand li south under the sun's bearing; earth and stars rise and fall in their four excursions within thirty thousand li — hence halving it yields the terrestrial center, which is now Yangcheng in Yingchuan."
translations.idiomatic: One chi and five cun marks the point fifteen thousand li south under the sun's bearing; earth and stars oscillate within thirty thousand li in their four excursions — halving this gives the terrestrial center, which is present-day Yangcheng in Yingchuan."

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉中，南征林邑，五月立表望之，日在表北，交州影在表南三寸，林邑九寸一分。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Song, during the southern campaign against Linyi, in the fifth month a gnomon was erected and observed: the sun stood north of the gnomon; at Jiaozhou the shadow fell three cun south of the gnomon, at Linyi nine cun and one fen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanjia era of Song, on the southern campaign against Linyi, a gnomon was erected in the fifth month: the sun stood north of the gnomon. At Jiaozhou the shadow fell three cun south of the gnomon; at Linyi, nine cun and one fen.

sentences.zh: 交州去洛，水陸之路九千里，蓋山川回折使之然，以表考其弦當五千乎。

translations.literal: Jiaozhou is nine thousand li from Luoyang by water and land routes — likely because mountains and rivers bend and turn make it so; measured by the gnomon, the straight chord should be about five thousand, perhaps.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou lies nine thousand li from Luoyang by water and land routes — the winding terrain surely accounts for the distance — but measured by the gnomon, the straight chord should be about five thousand li.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年，測交州，夏至，在表南三寸三分，與元嘉所測略同。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan, Jiaozhou was measured: at the summer solstice, the shadow fell three cun and three fen south of the gnomon, roughly the same as the Yuanjia measurement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan, Jiaozhou was measured again: at the summer solstice the shadow fell three cun and three fen south of the gnomon — roughly the same as the Yuanjia figure.

sentences.zh: 使者大相元太言：「交州望極，才高二十餘度。

translations.literal: The envoy Da Xiangyuan Tai said: "Gazing at the pole from Jiaozhou, it stands barely more than twenty degrees high.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy Da Xiangyuan Tai reported: "Viewed from Jiaozhou, the pole stands barely twenty-odd degrees above the horizon.

sentences.zh: 八月海中望老人星下列星粲然，明大者甚眾，古所未識，乃渾天家以為常沒地中者也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, gazing at sea, the stars below the Old Man Star shone brilliantly; very many were bright and large, never recognized in antiquity — those that armillary-heaven scholars hold are constantly sunk below the earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, looking out to sea, the stars below Canopus blazed brilliantly — many large and bright, unknown to antiquity — the very stars that armillary-heaven scholars say lie permanently below the earth.

sentences.zh: 大率去南極二十度已上之星則見。

translations.literal: In general, stars more than twenty degrees from the south pole become visible.
translations.idiomatic: In general, stars more than twenty degrees from the south pole become visible.

sentences.zh: 」又鐵勒、回紇在薛延陀之北，去京師六千九百里，其北又有骨利幹，居澣海之北，北距大海，晝長而夜短，既夜，天如曛不暝，夕胹羊髀才熟而曙，蓋近日出沒之所。

translations.literal: " Again, Tiele and Uighur lie north of Xueyantuo, six thousand nine hundred li from the capital; farther north still is Guligan, dwelling north of the Han Sea, with the great sea to the north. Days are long and nights short; even at night the sky is like dusk and does not darken; roast lamb shanks are barely done at evening when dawn comes — surely near where the sun rises and sets.
translations.idiomatic: " The Tiele and Uighur peoples lay north of Xueyantuo, six thousand nine hundred li from the capital. Farther north still lived the Guligan, north of the Han Sea with the ocean beyond. Days were long and nights short; even at night the sky glowed like dusk without full darkness, and lamb shanks roasted at evening were barely done before dawn — surely near the place where the sun rises and sets.

sentences.zh: 太史監南宮說擇河南平地，設水準繩墨植表而以引度之，自滑台始白馬，夏至之晷，尺五寸七分。

translations.literal: Grand Clerk Supervisor Nangong Shuo selected level ground in Henan, set leveling cords and ink lines, erected gnomons, and measured by successive steps: starting from Baima at Huatai, the summer solstice gnomon shadow was one chi, five cun, and seven fen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Clerk Supervisor Nangong Shuo selected level ground in Henan, set leveling cords and ink lines, erected gnomons, and measured in successive stages. Starting from Baima at Huatai, the summer solstice shadow measured one chi, five cun, and seven fen.

sentences.zh: 又南百九十八里百七十九步，得浚儀嶽台，晷尺五寸三分。

translations.literal: Another one hundred ninety-eight li and one hundred seventy-nine paces south yielded the Yue Terrace at Junyi; the gnomon shadow one chi, five cun, and three fen.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred ninety-eight li and one hundred seventy-nine paces farther south, at the Yue Terrace in Junyi, the shadow was one chi, five cun, and three fen.

sentences.zh: 又南百六十七里二百八十一步，得扶溝，晷尺四寸四分。

translations.literal: Another one hundred sixty-seven li and two hundred eighty-one paces south yielded Fugou; the gnomon shadow one chi, four cun, and four fen.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred sixty-seven li and two hundred eighty-one paces farther south, at Fugou, the shadow was one chi, four cun, and four fen.

sentences.zh: 又南百六十里百一十步，至上蔡武津，晷尺三寸六分半。

translations.literal: Another one hundred sixty li and one hundred ten paces south yielded Wujin at Shangcai; the gnomon shadow one chi, three cun, six fen, and a half.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred sixty li and one hundred ten paces farther south, at Wujin in Shangcai, the shadow was one chi, three cun, six fen, and a half.

sentences.zh: 大率五百二十六里二百七十步，晷差二寸餘。

translations.literal: In general, for every five hundred twenty-six li and two hundred seventy paces, the gnomon shadow differed by slightly more than two cun.
translations.idiomatic: On average, the shadow differed by slightly more than two cun for every five hundred twenty-six li and two hundred seventy paces.

sentences.zh: 而舊說王畿千里，影差一寸，妄矣。

translations.literal: The old claim that within the royal domain a thousand li makes one cun of shadow difference was false.
translations.idiomatic: The old claim that within the royal domain the shadow differed one cun per thousand li was plainly wrong.

sentences.zh: 今以句股校陽城中晷，夏至尺四寸七分八厘，冬至丈二尺七寸一分半，定春秋分五尺四寸三分，以覆矩斜視，極出地三十四度十分度之四。

translations.literal: Now by right triangle verification of the noon gnomon shadow at Yangcheng: summer solstice one chi, four cun, seven fen, and eight li; winter solstice one zhang, two chi, seven cun, one fen, and a half; fixed spring and autumn equinox five chi, four cun, and three fen; by inverted square and oblique sighting, the pole rises thirty-four and four-tenths degrees above the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Triangulating the noon shadows at Yangcheng gives a summer solstice shadow of one chi, four cun, seven fen, and eight li; a winter solstice shadow of one zhang, two chi, seven cun, one fen, and a half; and fixed equinox shadows of five chi, four cun, and three fen. By inverted square and oblique sighting, the pole rises thirty-four and four-tenths degrees above the horizon.

sentences.zh: 自滑台表視之，極高三十五度三分，冬至丈三尺，定春秋分五尺五寸六分。

translations.literal: Viewed from the gnomon at Huatai, the pole stands thirty-five and three-tenths degrees high; winter solstice one zhang and three chi; fixed spring and autumn equinox five chi, five cun, and six fen.
translations.idiomatic: From the Huatai gnomon, the pole stands thirty-five and three-tenths degrees high; the winter solstice shadow, one zhang and three chi; the fixed equinox shadow, five chi, five cun, and six fen.

sentences.zh: 自浚儀錶視之，極高三十四度八分，冬至丈二尺八寸五分，定春秋分五尺五寸。

translations.literal: Viewed from the gnomon at Junyi, the pole stands thirty-four and eight-tenths degrees high; winter solstice one zhang, two chi, eight cun, and five fen; fixed spring and autumn equinox five chi and five cun.
translations.idiomatic: From the Junyi gnomon, the pole stands thirty-four and eight-tenths degrees high; the winter solstice shadow, one zhang, two chi, eight cun, and five fen; the fixed equinox shadow, five chi and five cun.

sentences.zh: 知扶溝表視之，極高三十四度三分，冬至丈二尺五寸五分，定春秋分五尺三寸七分。

translations.literal: Viewed from the gnomon at Fugou, the pole stands thirty-four and three-tenths degrees high; winter solstice one zhang, two chi, five cun, and five fen; fixed spring and autumn equinox five chi, three cun, and seven fen.
translations.idiomatic: From the Fugou gnomon, the pole stands thirty-four and three-tenths degrees high; the winter solstice shadow, one zhang, two chi, five cun, and five fen; the fixed equinox shadow, five chi, three cun, and seven fen.

sentences.zh: 上蔡武津表視之，極高三十三度八分，冬至丈二尺三寸八分，定春秋分五尺二寸八分。

translations.literal: Viewed from the gnomon at Wujin in Shangcai, the pole stands thirty-three and eight-tenths degrees high; winter solstice one zhang, two chi, three cun, and eight fen; fixed spring and autumn equinox five chi, two cun, and eight fen.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wujin gnomon in Shangcai, the pole stands thirty-three and eight-tenths degrees high; the winter solstice shadow, one zhang, two chi, three cun, and eight fen; the fixed equinox shadow, five chi, two cun, and eight fen.

sentences.zh: 其北極去地，雖秒分微有盈縮，難以目校，大率三百五十一里八十步，而極差一度。

translations.literal: The north pole's distance from the earth, though seconds and parts slightly expand and contract and are hard to verify by eye, in general differs one degree for every three hundred fifty-one li and eighty paces.
translations.idiomatic: The pole's altitude, though fine seconds and parts vary slightly beyond what the eye can verify, differs by one degree for roughly every three hundred fifty-one li and eighty paces.

sentences.zh: 極之遠近異，則黃道軌景固隨而變矣。

translations.literal: When the pole's distance differs, the ecliptic track and gnomon shadows naturally change accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: As the pole's altitude changes, the ecliptic track and gnomon shadows naturally change with it.

sentences.zh: 自此為率推之，比歲武陵晷，夏至七寸七分，冬至丈五寸三分，春秋分四尺三寸七分半，以圖測之，定氣四尺四寸七分，按圖斜視，極高二十九度半，差陽城五度三分。

translations.literal: Extrapolating from this ratio, comparing with Wuling's gnomon shadows that year: summer solstice seven cun and seven fen, winter solstice one zhang, five cun, and three fen, spring and autumn equinox four chi, three cun, seven fen, and a half; measured on the diagram, fixed qi four chi, four cun, and seven fen; by oblique sighting on the diagram, the pole stands twenty-nine and a half degrees high, five and three-tenths degrees less than Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating from this ratio to Wuling's shadows that year: summer solstice, seven cun and seven fen; winter solstice, one zhang, five cun, and three fen; equinox, four chi, three cun, seven fen, and a half. Measured on the diagram, the fixed-qi shadow is four chi, four cun, and seven fen; by oblique sighting, the pole stands twenty-nine and a half degrees — five and three-tenths degrees lower than at Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 蔚州橫野軍夏至二尺二寸九分，冬至丈五尺八寸九分，春秋分六尺四寸四分半，以圖測之，定氣六尺六寸二分半。

translations.literal: At Hengye Army in Weizhou: summer solstice two chi, two cun, and nine fen; winter solstice one zhang, five chi, eight cun, and nine fen; spring and autumn equinox six chi, four cun, four fen, and a half; measured on the diagram, fixed qi six chi, six cun, two fen, and a half.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengye Army in Weizhou: summer solstice shadow, two chi, two cun, and nine fen; winter solstice, one zhang, five chi, eight cun, and nine fen; equinox, six chi, four cun, four fen, and a half. Measured on the diagram, the fixed-qi shadow is six chi, six cun, two fen, and a half.

sentences.zh: 按圖斜視，極高四十度，差陽城五度三分。

translations.literal: By oblique sighting on the diagram, the pole stands forty degrees high, five and three-tenths degrees more than Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: By oblique sighting on the diagram, the pole stands forty degrees — five and three-tenths degrees higher than at Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 凡南北之差十度半，其徑三千六百八十里九十步。

translations.literal: In all, the north-south difference is ten and a half degrees; the diameter is three thousand six hundred eighty li and ninety paces.
translations.idiomatic: The total north-south difference is ten and a half degrees, spanning a diameter of three thousand six hundred eighty li and ninety paces.

sentences.zh: 自陽城至武陵，千八百二十六里七十六步；

translations.literal: From Yangcheng to Wuling, one thousand eight hundred twenty-six li and seventy-six paces;
translations.idiomatic: From Yangcheng to Wuling is one thousand eight hundred twenty-six li and seventy-six paces;

sentences.zh: 自陽城至橫野，千八百六十一里二百十四步。

translations.literal: from Yangcheng to Hengye, one thousand eight hundred sixty-one li and two hundred fourteen paces.
translations.idiomatic: from Yangcheng to Hengye, one thousand eight hundred sixty-one li and two hundred fourteen paces.

sentences.zh: 夏至晷差尺五寸三分；

translations.literal: The summer solstice gnomon shadow difference is one chi, five cun, and three fen;
translations.idiomatic: The total summer solstice shadow difference is one chi, five cun, and three fen;

sentences.zh: 自陽城至武陵，差七寸三分；

translations.literal: from Yangcheng to Wuling, the difference is seven cun and three fen;
translations.idiomatic: from Yangcheng to Wuling, seven cun and three fen;

sentences.zh: 自陽城至橫野，差八寸。

translations.literal: from Yangcheng to Hengye, the difference is eight cun.
translations.idiomatic: from Yangcheng to Hengye, eight cun.

sentences.zh: 冬至晷差五尺三寸六分，自陽城至武陵差二尺一寸八分；

translations.literal: The winter solstice gnomon shadow difference is five chi, three cun, and six fen; from Yangcheng to Wuling the difference is two chi, one cun, and eight fen;
translations.idiomatic: The total winter solstice shadow difference is five chi, three cun, and six fen; from Yangcheng to Wuling, two chi, one cun, and eight fen;

sentences.zh: 自陽城至橫野，差三尺一寸八分。

translations.literal: from Yangcheng to Hengye, the difference is three chi, one cun, and eight fen.
translations.idiomatic: from Yangcheng to Hengye, three chi, one cun, and eight fen.

sentences.zh: 率夏至與南方差少，冬至與北方差多。

translations.literal: In ratio, the summer solstice difference with the south is less, the winter solstice difference with the north is greater.
translations.idiomatic: On average, the summer solstice shadow varies less toward the south, while the winter solstice shadow varies more toward the north.

sentences.zh: 又以圖校安南，日在天頂北二度四分，極高二十度四分。

translations.literal: Again, by diagram verification of Annam: the sun stands two and four-tenths degrees north of the zenith; the pole stands twenty and four-tenths degrees high.
translations.idiomatic: The diagram was also used to verify Annam: the sun stands two and four-tenths degrees north of the zenith, and the pole twenty and four-tenths degrees above the horizon.

sentences.zh: 冬至晷七尺九寸四分，定春秋分二尺九寸三分，夏至在表南三寸三分，差陽城十四度三分，其徑五千二十三里。

translations.literal: Winter solstice gnomon shadow seven chi, nine cun, and four fen; fixed spring and autumn equinox two chi, nine cun, and three fen; summer solstice shadow three cun and three fen south of the gnomon; fourteen and three-tenths degrees less than Yangcheng; the diameter is five thousand twenty-three li.
translations.idiomatic: The winter solstice shadow is seven chi, nine cun, and four fen; the fixed equinox shadow, two chi, nine cun, and three fen; the summer solstice shadow falls three cun and three fen south of the gnomon. The pole stands fourteen and three-tenths degrees lower than at Yangcheng, across a diameter of five thousand twenty-three li.

sentences.zh: 至林邑，日在天頂北六度六分強，極高十七度四分，周圓三十五度，常見不隱。

translations.literal: At Linyi, the sun stands slightly more than six and six-tenths degrees north of the zenith; the pole stands seventeen and four-tenths degrees high; the circumpolar circuit thirty-five degrees — constantly visible, never hidden.
translations.idiomatic: At Linyi, the sun stands slightly more than six and six-tenths degrees north of the zenith; the pole, seventeen and four-tenths degrees high. Stars within thirty-five degrees of the pole are constantly visible and never set.

sentences.zh: 冬至晷六尺九寸，定春秋分二尺八寸五分，夏至在表南五寸七分，其徑六千一百一十二里。

translations.literal: Winter solstice gnomon shadow six chi and nine cun; fixed spring and autumn equinox two chi, eight cun, and five fen; summer solstice shadow five cun and seven fen south of the gnomon; the diameter is six thousand one hundred twelve li.
translations.idiomatic: The winter solstice shadow is six chi and nine cun; the fixed equinox shadow, two chi, eight cun, and five fen; the summer solstice shadow falls five cun and seven fen south of the gnomon. The diameter spans six thousand one hundred twelve li.

sentences.zh: 若令距陽城而北，至鐵勒之地，亦差十七度四分，與林邑正等，則五月日在天頂南二十七度四分，極高五十二度，周圓百四度，常見不隱。
